NarrativeText: In October 2023, the Magnox Swarf Storage Silos (MSSS) Retrievals Programme received re-sanctioning approval, establishing an overall upper funding limit of £1,098m. As part of that endorsement, a revised management framework and sanctioning strategy was introduced to govern the MSSS 2nd Extension (2E) & 3rd Extension (3E) Tranche, as discrete projects. These projects are delivering critical enablers that will facilitate the commencement of waste retrieval operations from Silo Emptying Plant (SEP) 3. They have an upper sanction limit of £200m. The key enablers included are 1) SEP3; Complete design/rectification, installation and commissioning of the machine and associated components. 2) Final manufacture and installation scope for the Nitrogen Inlet system. 3) 2E Liquor Level management system.  4) The remaining Packages required to support full retrievals. The programme has prioritised the OB/FE and as a result the expected specialist resources (e.g. design capability) will not be available to concurrently deliver SEP3. Without further action the delivery will take substantially longer, challenging tolerances. To address this SL is pursuing an alternative delivery model with a fully integrated programme partner that is expected to increase efficiency and critically access a different part of the skill market we have previously failed to harness. As Nuclear Decommissioning Solutions have now been appointed as Lot 3 partner we are working on the alternative delivery strategy. This appears credible with a significant opportunity to protect or improve the schedule. Therefore the Delivery Confidence Assessment remains Amber. There has been no change to the EAC during this period. The project remains in the early stages of its lifecycle, with only six of the nine 2E/3E projects sanctioned, and a total released value of £64.4m. While future cost and schedule pressures are anticipated, the project is forecasting lifecycle EAC within the sanctioned upper limit of £200m and to timelines that align with the critical path of the Magnox Swarf Storage Silo (MSSS) Programme and as such, no direct impact is expected on sustained retrievals. The capability and capacity RAG is Red driven by resource constraints and commercial disruption following the administration of a key supply chain partner. In response, the integrated team is actively working with administrators to recover part-manufactured equipment, having identified secure interim storage, and identified a replacement supplier to complete outstanding packages, with direct award contract placements expected next period. This disruption has led to increased in-year expenditure due to associated recovery and transition costs. The Baseline RAG status is Amber, reflecting anticipated impacts from ongoing commercial challenges and supply chain, but also in acknowledgement of the recovery plan currently being enacted by the project team to ensure delivery of packages in support of the programme requirements.

The Electrical Distribution Network Upgrade Project (EDNUP) relates to the refurbishment of the Sellafield Site’s electricity network. The project will bolster the emergency power generation capability and improve site resilience which is important particularly in the event of a National Grid failure. The Delivery Confidence Assessment remains at Amber noting that the latest forecast for completion exceeds the current P80.  An update paper was acknowledged at NDA GIC in June 2025, which noted that a P80 draw down will be necessary  to enable continuity of project delivery (current forecast required in 2026/27 Q1).  The full lifecycle cost forecast is stable in period although under significant increasing pressure from strike delay costs and further realised risks with in-ground conditions and increases in subcontract costs.  The further review of the P50 to P80 delta and inflationary impact will be included in the next sanction request.  The schedule is stable with no overall movement to the end date in period, although realised risks and strike action are impacting schedule float. The baseline RAG remains Amber as the project completion date is beyond the P50 baseline. The current P50 baseline and approved NDA sanction differs as a result of indexation and historical positive cost variance on the project pre implementation of change control associated with the Full Business Case (FBC) resubmission. The project plan and progress to date indicates a steady recovery of the variance.  Grid Transformer 2 has now been re-energised and grid power is now available to the new Sub111, which is the first new substation asset to be delivered by EDNUP, with grid connection allowing for future asset risk reduction benefits . Cable route construction is progressing on multiple fronts, including a ringfenced risk mitigation advanced dig team who are discovering a significant number of uncharted services and obstructions. Reoccurrences of radiological contamination are hindering interconnector critical path progress and causing reducing overall project float. A peer assist has identified opportunities to improve delivery arrangements in future changeover stages and interconnector delivery, which will be developed over the coming periods.   Strike action has impacted several workfaces including the temporary cable installation which will mitigate delays to electrical isolations necessary for excavations near aged buried cables.  Management and characterisation of waste from the site continues to be onerous.  The Capability and Capacity RAG remains at Amber in period due to Pre-Operations, Construction and Protection Engineer resource issues, which are now becoming critical, with timescales for backfill still to be determined.

ProjectName: Box Encapsulation Plant Product Store Direct Import Facility
NarrativeText: BEPPS-DIF project is essential to remediation of Pile Fuel Cladding Silo (PFCS) and provides capability to receive and store waste from remediation work. PFCS boxes required for active commissioning all received in BEPPS-DIF. All physical activities relating to active commissioning now complete. Project is on close out of fault observations (FOBs) and remaining project scope. Duly Authorised Person (DAP) move to support Advanced Gas Reactor (AGR) / Encapsulated Product Store (EPS) transfers may challenge end date for commissioning and rectifying subsequent faults in parallel with plant operations. Project resources are substantially redeployed on other scope for Retrievals Operations keeping project spend to a minimum. Endorsement to operate is now planned for 31/03/2026. Delivery Confidence Assessment remains Amber. Baseline RAG remains Amber. Capability and Capacity RAG remains Green, project has resource to complete scope. The project completion date remains April 2026, which is aligned with the anticipated IRP date of the Post Investment Appraisal.

Full Retrievals Project 1 (FRP1) will provide capability to continue progress made in Pile Fuel Cladding Silo (PFCS) Early Retrievals Project and is delivering the first 5 of 18 scope areas required to complete Full Retrievals operations. The first project benefit is a reduction in radiological risk to workers, public and the environment, which is an overall programme benefit included in the FRP1 Business Case with a forecast date of 2030, which has been communicated via the Enterprise Benefit Register. The benefit can only be realised after the start of Full Retrievals operations, not only the completion of FRP1. P80 sanction approved 29th April 2024, taking cumulative sanction released to £74.6m “not to exceed value of £75m” for the re-scoped project at the request of NDA Accounting Officer. The Delivery Confidence Assessment remains Amber. This is based on the current forecast project end date of November 2025. The lifetime EAC remains at £72.5m, with the actual cost at completion to be confirmed next period, following close out of final accounting and Gate 5.  Baseline RAG also remains Amber, which reflects the current forecast end date of November 2025, 5 months later than current baseline. The P50 baseline is slightly greater than the sanction released due to indexation. In period the Post Investment Appraisal (PIA) was endorsed at PFCS Programme Board, with actions placed at Retrievals Portfolio Board to provide updates to the paper, and feedback for approval at Retrievals weekly team meeting. The gate 5 SPER was held on 21st October 2025, achieving a rating of Green for cost & schedule, and Amber for requirements and resources. There is no risk to project close-out on the basis that the amber ratings will be managed in the Programme’s forward strategy for full retrievals capability. The project is progressing the SPER findings and Retrievals Board actions ahead of the Readiness review, which would confirm readiness for PIA submission to the December Gated Project Oversight Committee (GPOC). Close out activities have not been impacted by the recent strike action. The Capability and Capacity RAG remains Green with no issues to report.

This project enables retrievals in Magnox Swarf Storage Silos (MSSS) Original Building and the 1st Extension. This includes completion of Silo Emptying Plant (SEP) 2 and SEP 1. The first project benefit was completed in 2022, enabling the successful start of Retrievals from SEP 2. The Delivery Confidence Assessment remains Amber in light of challenges to the SEP1 commissioning schedule, although in the context of the full project, issues appear resolvable and should not threaten P80 values. The project has reviewed assumptions underpinning the SEP 1 inactive and active commissioning and based on the feedback is taking steps to address perceived delivery gaps, including addressing potential inefficiencies in the approach to commissioning and pre-operations (teams shape and size, working patterns etc). Challenges in delivering commissioning tasks ahead of the SEP1 move between compartments later this year resulted in an impact on YE BCWP and additional commissioning resource usage resulted in an EAC increase in period. This flowed through to a minor movement of the planned first skip out date in November 2027. The Baseline RAG status remains Amber. This period, the project continued to deliver commissioning activities on SEP1, although efficiency was impacted by strike action.  On SEP2 raking was successfully completed, which has resulted in a level waste bed for retrievals later this FY.  The Project team also commenced a review to inform configuration management across SEP1 and SEP2, with a focus on the activities required to close out SEP2. The Vent project has continued to work through inactive commissioning scope, with utilities supporting next period for energisation of new capability in the Lateral Restraint Tower. Although there is a significant negative cost variance between the EAC and Baseline, £64.3m of this was historical (prior to 2022) and although included in the current sanction, is not included in the Baseline. The Capability and Capacity remains Green, based on the assumption that resources will be made available to support the prioritised Original Building/1st Extension scope. Design capability resource requests are to be submitted in November. Several programme requirements need to be delivered in parallel with the retrievals project scope to enable a full retrieval capability, this includes the Skip Fill Optimisation opportunity and key SEP Machine improvements such as to manage large items, deal with pressurised containers and manage waste craters. The project and programme are working together to minimise the impact of implementation of this scope, (which is additional to the sanctioned Business Case), on the project deliverables.

The SSAU project will provide infrastructure and equipment that will provide security and emergency response teams with a significantly improved capability to react to and manage security and/or emergency events on the Sellafield site. The first project benefit is equipment which, once operational in the command centre, will provide a significantly improved capability to react and manage security and/or emergency events on the Sellafield site - thereby complying with the standards, expectations and objectives set by nuclear regulators. The Delivery Confidence Assessment remains stable at Green recognising forecast delivery within the Projects P80 Sanction. The Baseline RAG has remained Red in period, as the Cost forecast remains beyond the P50 baseline. The Project is still however forecasting to deliver within the P80 Sanction released to Sellafield. In period the Lifecycle EAC has increased slightly, but still within the P80 Sanction, due to the Level 1 Commissioning Date and Legacy Building Migration moving out slightly from January 2026 to February 2026 due to minor technical issues found in commissioning and impact of the strikes leading to retention of commissioning resources for a further period.  In period good progress continues with commissioning with some issues delaying the work as they are resolved, the strike has reduce working time slightly each day but the team are working around this where possible.  The next stage of strikes will have an impact as scaffolding is required to access an area of fence which needs minor sensor repairs before commissioning.  The Amber rating on the Capability and Capacity RAG recognises that schedule adherence is reliant on skilled resources and the project team is now a very thin layer and any loss of resources would impact delivery.

The scope of the Heat Exchanger (HEx) Deplanting 1 project is the removal and laydown of the first 6 Calder Hall Heat Exchangers, as an enabler for land clearance in preparation for a new Site Ion Exchange Effluent Plant (SIXEP) operating facility; subsequent disposal of these initial 6 Heat Exchangers and the deplanting & disposal of the remaining 10 Heat Exchangers is out-with this project. The Delivery Confidence Assessment is Green, as both lifecycle costs and end date remain within the approved P80 position. The Baseline RAG has moved to Green following approval and implementation of a recent change control to align with the Business Case revised Commercial strategy (6 month delay with no change to scope/cost), December 2029 (P50) and December 2030 (P80) project completion dates are now confirmed. In period, the laydown area design continues to mature with an Interpretative report now received from the Boreholes work, which confirms assumptions made during the in parallel completion of key design documents.  Although a small amount of re-work is necessary, nothing fundamental has been identified and the project is anticipating design review completion by the end of December 2025, allowing enough time to place an Invitation To Tender (ITT) through the Decommissioning and Nuclear Waste Partnership (DNWP) framework by 2nd February 2026 (Ops plan milestone) which remains on target.  On the main lifting contract, as previously reported, the evaluations have been completed and a successful candidate identified.  Reviews prior to sign off of the evaluation report are ongoing which has delayed issue of the tender letters/standstill period of 7 days prior to contract award, this is now anticipated in Period 8 (award). Capability and Capacity, following the Change Control implementation, is now Green whilst the project work towards placement of the main HEx1 lifting contract.

The BEP Project provides the Magnox Swarf Storage Silos (MSSS) Programme the capability to receive, package, inspect, and transfer Intermediate Level Waste to interim stores. At completion, BEP will enable waste retrieval at pace, to maintain an As Low as Reasonably Practicable (ALARP) position, a fundamental requirement of Sellafield Ltd site license conditions.  The first project benefit: Regulatory approval to Start Active Commissioning is forecast 10th August 2027.  Estimated date for first MSSS box into BEP and Active Commissioning of MSSS waste is November 2027, with benefits realisation associated with the start of Operations April 2028.  Project Completion including governance is currently forecast as August 2028, within the period of ‘up to 12 months’ after the Start of Active Commissioning defined in the approved Resubmitted Business Case.  The Delivery Confidence Assessment (DCA) has changed to Amber to recognise the Project challenges that are being managed, the Baseline RAG remains Amber.  Lifetime EAC is beyond sanction P50 but within sanction P80 cost. The preparation of a P80 Drawdown is underway, targeting executive decisions by end of this calendar year.  There is no change in period to the Start Active Commissioning forecast and lifecycle EAC.  The project acknowledges pressure on the forecast P50 position following cost growth and schedule slippage in the deterministic Joint Venture (JV) EAC and programme from the impact of Fault Observations (FOBs) on critical path commissioning activities and on-going construction delays impacting the handover of Safety Transfer Certificates (STCs) to commissioning.   These delays reflect the projects strategic decision to target more complex STCs first with the majority of these STCs due to be delivered in the coming months. Whilst these delays have resulted in deterministic float erosion and caused a narrowing of the forecasted range (August to November 2027 and £1,445m to £1,475m) confidence remains in delivering within P80 parameters.  Highlights in period the handover of 250 STC (WTC Decontamination & Maintenance) from Construction to Commissioning achieved .  Grout Plant Engineering Orders (EOs) and Technical Requisitions (TRs) complete.  The Capability and Capacity status remains Green this period as the project continues the transition from Construction to Commissioning, with resource transition plans developed.

ProjectName: Sellafield Product & Residue Store Retreatment Plant
NarrativeText: The Sellafield Product & Residue Store Retreatment Plant (SRP) project is a key element of the Sellafield Ltd ‘Special Nuclear Materials (SNM) Future State Programme’. The SRP is a complex major project required to provide the capability to receive special nuclear material in existing packages, from existing stores on the Sellafield site, and process the material into a form and package suitable for safe and secure long-term interim storage. The SRO Delivery Confidence Assessment (DCA) has moved from Green to Amber against the P80 cost and schedule from the Full Business Case (FBC) approved by HMG in July 2021. This is primarily reflective of the previously reported emerging issue relating to legislative changes to Passive Fire Protection standards, following the implementation of the Building Safety Act 2022. This Act represents a major regulatory shift in the UK construction industry, particularly in fire safety aiming to improve accountability and safety following the Grenfell Tower Inquiry. The impact of the Passive Fire Protection standards will require a significant amount of engineering design rework and additional installation work in the facility; the main impact is expected to be on the timescales to achieve readiness of the facility for Glove box installation, which has now become the critical path. The initial assessment has been carried out and is currently being quantified and assured and an assessment is also being made as to how this issue should be considered in terms of the projects current P80 sanctioned cost and schedule.  Additionally, as previously reported the project has been impacted by extraordinary inflation incurred to date. Following the DESNZ PIC decision in Q2 24/25 to postpone the £164.6m Inflation Sanction relief, the project has had to absorb inflationary costs using its existing contingency. As a result, £128.9m of the P50–P80 sanctioned contingency has been utilised, leaving £190m remaining. This erosion of contingency increases the likelihood of a future re-sanction request for additional P50–P80 funding, particularly as further events may arise that impact the remaining contingency. The project will be requesting P80 cost and schedule relief to DESNZ PIC when appropriate. Key recommendations and actions from the last Gate 0/ Annual Review have been addressed and a review of the effectiveness of the close out actions will be carried out in Quarter 4. These  included the requirement to ensure sufficient design engineering resource was in place to support safety case, and mitigation of the risk of delays relating to furnace manufacture (impacting installation of both Glove Boxes and MEICA equipment). The Capability and Capacity RAG status remains Amber with ongoing challenges in recruitment principally across several disciplines including construction, engineering, commissioning, and quality. Finally, the successful active commissioning and future operations of the SRP facility are contingent upon several dependencies managed within the SNM Future State Programme. A critical dependency is the availability of SNM analytical capability, which is essential to support both commissioning and ongoing operational activities. To address this, a dedicated project is being developed and delivered through the PPP to ensure the required analytical capability is in place. The SNM Future State Programme team is responsible for managing all dependencies associated with SRP, with the overarching goal of ensuring that all necessary capabilities are aligned and available to enable the delivery of SRP outcomes and the realisation of associated benefits.

The Civil Nuclear Constabulary (CNC) Operational Unit project will provide one location on site to house all CNC personnel, with space allowance for future uplift of officers, whilst mitigating health and safety risks associated with the current facilities. The Delivery Confidence Assessment (DCA) is stable at Green as the Resubmission Full Business Case (FBC) has received approval from His Majesty’s Treasury (HMT) in June 2024. Bulk Construction is nearing completion but has been delayed until November, in part due to strike action and reprioritisation of resources to complete critical path works in the Level 1 Board rooms.  The completion of the Level 1 Board rooms was initially impacted by the replacement of the non-complaint glands, has been further impacted by the strike action as well as slower than anticipated progress of the other works required to be completed and higher level of snagging than anticipated following contractor and client inspections.  These delays have been compounded through the loss of opportunity to recover through additional weekend working due the Union imposed overtime ban related to the on-going industrial action. The completion and commissioning of the Level 1 Boards is the enabler for the release of all future commissioning works.  CNSL with support of Amentum Executives, have explored the opportunity to exploit the 120-day duration for Commissioning and Handover, this has seen more efficient planning of the commissioning phase, reducing the duration from 120 days to 93 days to maintain current forecast end date. On-site work continues to progress well, civils scope is focused on external works and building finishes, Control, Electrical & Instrumentation (CE&I) works is focused on ensuring the Level 1 boards are ready for commissioning with the Project working closely with Utilities. Heat, Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) installation works is almost complete. The Capability and Capacity RAG remains Green for the period with no current vacancies.

The ILW EZ Phase 1 Excavation Project is a key enabler to allow the future major project Lightly Shielded Store 1 (LSS1) to commence construction and also de-risks LSS1 construction. The delays in issuing the Service Commencement Notification (SCN) and late Pre-Construction Information (PCI) caused a 4-month delay to the beginning of delivery, however the excavation work has now recovered. The first project benefit: This project delivers a number of benefits, both direct as a key enabler for LSS1, and indirect in adopting an Enterprise approach to zonal development. The Baseline remains green.  All issues have now been rectified.  All works are now complete and awaiting isolations to be removed before sign off. Walk rounds have taken place and a meeting to arrange the CTC transfer is being set up. Lifecycle EAC and the forecast date for close out of the Project remain stable. The Capability and Capacity RAG remains Green.

The SIXEP Continuity Plant (SCP) is required to deliver a continued site effluent treatment capability in support of radioactive liquid effluent discharge permits, fuel pond management, high hazard reduction projects and the overall NDA mission. This project provides a replacement for the existing SIXEP Sea Discharge Treatment plant and is therefore mission critical to the safe operation of the site. The SRO Delivery Confidence Assessment (DCA) currently remains green however there is a significant risk posed by the impact of extraordinary inflation that has been incurred to date. This follows the decision made by PIC in Q2 24/25 to not approve the P80 Inflation Sanction relief for SCP. The NDA have released £108.7m sanction to SL from P80 as an interim measure to deal with the inflation impact, however this substantially erodes the P80 contingency. The first scope driven P80 drawdown for the project has been approved this quarter.  Combined, these two drawdowns result in a net £31M P80 contingency remaining. The SRO considers that this is likely to be insufficient for the next 4 years and has submitted a sanction release paper to the Department in September, with review pending.  Without this additional sanction the current DCA rating would change from Green to Red, hence this will be kept under review by the SRO throughout 2025/26. From a project performance perspective, the SRO DCA remains Green, echoed by National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority (NISTA) Green rating received in June 25/26. The Baseline RAG remains Green. Fabrication of off-site pipework planned for completion Q4 25/26. Site pipework and vessel install is progressing well in both the Effluent Treatment Cell (ETC) and Bulk Storage Tank (BST) cells. Both halves of the reception pumping tank now in position and welding has commenced within the ETC, marking another significant milestone for the project. marking another milestone for the project. Works continue to progress across all floors within the Service Building prior to handover over to Mechanical, Electrical, Instrumentation, Control & Automation (MEICA) trades. Bulk Storage Tanks – welding of the first tank continues to progress in cell. Project Wide Objectives - PWO4 - Handover of BST cell to Commissioning,  PWO5 - Handover Services Building to Commissioning and PWO6 - Handover of ETC to Commissioning are all currently forecasting to be delayed with further impending strike action (Industrial Relations issues) however, these are not a threat to the critical path and project remains within P50. The last milestone on the journey is commencement of active commissioning (licence instrument approvals). Post scope driven P80 drawdown impact the baseline date is now 22nd July 2030 (P50) along with the P50 Lifecycle baseline end date moving to 21st October 2031. The forecast dates and lifecycle EAC remain stable.  The Capability and Capacity RAG remains Green with no issues to report.

The Box Encapsulation Plant Product Store 2 (BEPPS2) is a critical enabler for continued high hazard retrievals from the Magnox Swarf Storage Silo (MSSS) and Pile Fuel Cladding Silo (PFCS). It will provide modern, safe and secure long term interim storage for approximately 7,500 packages of Intermediate Level Waste. The strategic requirement has been confirmed. The first project benefit is the ability to receive packages from MSSS and PFCS without constraining hazard reduction programmes. The Senior Responsible Owner (SRO) Delivery Confidence Assessment is Green and the project remains on track against its P50 cost and schedule targets. The project is in the Define Phase, progressing detailed design for transition to civil construction and procurement of long-lead items. The critical path runs through civil construction, mechanical and electrical installation, and commissioning. A sub-critical path flows through the Multi-Disciplinary Design Review (MDDR), which will confirm design maturity and support release of the Outline Business Case (OBC) sanction hold point. The MDDR will be held during Period 8. Engagement with Programme and Project Partnership (PPP) Key Delivery Partners is ongoing to underpin delivery phase planning, cost estimation, and Quantitative Risk Analysis (QRA), informing the Full Business Case (FBC) submission planned for FY2026/27. Site establishment and bulk excavation works are progressing well. The civil construction contract delivery strategy is under review by PPP to ensure value for money. The SPI reflects both historic design delays due to historic resource constraints and the non-utilisation of risk and estimating uncertainty. The forthcoming OBC sanction hold point release submission (January 2026 to IRP & GIC and March 2026 to DESNZ PIC) will include updates on the lifecycle cost estimates that will be underpinned by an updated QRA and will reflect proactive management of opportunities and realisation of threats during the Define Stage. Capability RAG remains Green.

The Sellafield Security Enhancement Programme (SSEP) represents a series of interdependent security enhancement projects, which encompass site-wide improvement initiatives, and some facility-specific asset improvements. The Delivery Confidence Assessment remains Green. The NDA revised Programme Business Case value of £921.8m was released to SL in June 2024, with Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) PIC holding the upper range figure of £929.8m. The SSAU and CNC OU P80 sanction request submissions were approved at the NDA Group Investment Committee (GIC) in September 2024. The assessment work on Encrypted Comms project is complete resulting in a significant reduction in the project scope. The project EAC has therefore been reduced accordingly. Formal governance steps will conclude during period 8. The programme lifecycle EAC has therefore been reduced to reflect the EC position. The Programme Ready for FOC, based on the latest SSAU project data, remains forecast as March 2026 due to delays to the progression of the Legacy SMS migrations, which are scheduled to take place after the L1 commissioning of the new boundaries.. This is subject to ongoing reviews of the available operational, engineering and maintenance resources needed to review and sign off the various systems and assets being delivered by the projects to underpin the Custody Transfer Certificate (CTC). The overall outturn project delivery performance remains in line with sanctioned plans. Security Systems Architecture Upgrade (SSAU), Encrypted Comms (EC) & Civil Nuclear Constabulary (CNC) Operational Unit (CNC OU) Projects (all reported as projects in their own right on the MPPR) are, based on the respective projects latest EAC figures, affordable within the released SSEP sanction. The Main Site Command Facility (MSCF) continues to improve its operational capability with Phases 1 & 2 of the revised 3 Phase Capability Delivery Plan now complete. (Phase 1: The High Security Area (HSA)1 Boundary declared operational in March 2024 & Phase 2: The achievement of a Green rating for the complex and challenging Level 1 Regulator Evaluated Demonstration Exercise in November 2024). As a consequence the Regulator confirmed in December 2024, Physical Security no longer needs to be monitored at the “Enhanced Level” and has therefore been returned to “Routine Level” with the Nuclear Site Security Plan (NSSP) and Security Improvement Schedule (SIS) updated accordingly; a significant achievement for the Sellafield Site. Phase 3 will achieve the agreed security outcomes and associated security risk reduction benefits by no later than May 2027 for Full Operating Capability (FOC). The latest programme forecast aligns with the current CNC OU P80 sanction date of 31 July 2026. The programme remains within its sanctioned tolerances.
